title: Weekewackmamish (Mill Creek)
summary: Weekewackmamish is Mill Creek at Southport in Southampton, emptying into Peconic Bay.
history_content: The creek appears in Paucamp's testimony about Peconic Bay waterways and in a later deposition describing where local Native people gathered flags for mats. Dated records appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as where we cut reeds, or a place where reeds, rushes, or flags were gathered and cut.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are cultural artifacts that tell us as much about how people lived as do relics dug from the ground.”

— Virgil J. Vogel, Indian Names on Wisconsin's Map (1991), publisher description
preservation_content: Weekewackmamish preserves a working waterway name tied to plant gathering, mat making, and Peconic Bay creek knowledge.
whereintheworld_content: Blue/general approximate marker in the Southport/Hampton Bays Peconic Bay creek landscape. This is not an exact Mill Creek mouth or boundary coordinate.
